input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "invariant",
 "proof_obligation": "preservation",
 "diagnosis": "The bounds invariant `0 <= i <= a.Length + 1` is too weak. Dafny checks that the second invariant `forall x :: 0 <= x < i ==> cmp(a[x], max)` is well-formed in any loop-head state allowed by the earlier invariants, including i == a.Length + 1. In that state x == a.Length is in range of the quantifier, so a[x] is out of bounds (counterexample: a.Length = 1, x = 1). The loop really only reaches i == a.Length, so the bound should be `0 <= i <= a.Length`. That keeps a[x] in bounds for x < i and is preserved by the body, because i < a.Length before the increment."}
EOF
sed -i 's/invariant 0 <= i <= (a.Length) + 1/invariant 0 <= i <= a.Length/' program.dfy && dafny verify program.dfy

content.text:
program.dfy now verifies: Dafny reports `2 verified, 0 errors`.

**What was wrong:** the loop invariant's upper bound on `i` was too loose. Line 15 said `0 <= i <= (a.Length) + 1`. Dafny checks that each invariant makes sense in any state the earlier invariants allow, and this bound allowed `i == a.Length + 1`. In that state, the next invariant (`forall x :: 0 <= x < i ==> cmp(a[x], max)`) would read `a[a.Length]`, which is past the end of the array. That matches the counterexample: `a.Length = 1`, so `a[1]` is out of range. I recorded this in diagnosis.json as an invariant / preservation failure.

**Fix:** I changed line 15 to `invariant 0 <= i <= a.Length`. The loop never gets past `i == a.Length` anyway, because the body only runs while `i < a.Length` and adds 1. So the tighter bound still holds after each pass, keeps `a[x]` in range, and still proves the postcondition when the loop exits. I didn't change any other part of the specification.

The command exited with code 2 even though verification passed. That's because `dafny verify` treats warnings as errors when it tries to compile. The three warnings were already in the file: two unneeded semicolons on lines 4–5, and an `a != null` check that is always true. They don't affect verification, so I left them alone.
